title: Umi, a terminal for working with agents
description: Keep Claude and Codex sessions in panes alongside the Markdown you’re editing.
body: Umi is a macOS terminal with tabs, split panes and a Markdown editor. Each agent pane shows its session state. The command-line interface lets a session move panes and open a document in the editor.

title: Collect comments in one paste
description: Quote a selection, add a comment, and keep reading.
body: The Hammerspoon module binds Option+C to a small comment box. Each note keeps its selected passage. The clipboard accumulates them so the whole set can go into one message.

title: A map of a recurring process
description: Compare what AI handles today with what it could take on next.
body: This single-file dashboard takes a structured list of tasks and groups them by phase. It opens with suggested tasks to try, shows the assumptions behind the ratings, and can export a shareable copy. A fictional application round illustrates the format.

title: Ask a colleague’s AI a question
description: Reusable instructions for letting someone run a question against their own work and check the answer.
body: The template separates the question from four shared guides. Those guides cover where to look, how to write the report, what to leave out and how to hand the result back to the person who ran it.

title: A portable reader for an AI report
description: Turn a structured answer and its supporting quotes into one HTML file.
body: The viewer reads report data embedded in the file. Readers can move between sections with the arrow keys, expand quotes, and inspect which sources the report used or missed. The public copy starts empty.

title: What changes the shape of AI adoption?
description: An interactive notebook about the assumptions inside adoption curves.
body: Compare a model in which only some tasks are reachable with models in which tasks differ in difficulty or adoption encourages more adoption. The notebook lets you see how coaching changes each curve. The curves illustrate assumptions rather than measured effects.

title: Pacing calls in five-minute blocks
description: A floating Mac clock with a ring that fills once every five minutes.
body: I built a small clock that stays above a call window. The ring shows progress through the current five-minute block and the counter shows how many blocks have passed.

title: A one-page verdict for a tool trial
description: Choose the question before testing, then record where the tool works and fails.
body: A reusable brief records the decision, versions, test cases and completion condition. The verdict template pairs each result with a run. Standard cases include rich documents, concurrent edits and a read–write round trip.

title: Testing Claude’s Google Docs connector
description: The test fixture and recorded runs behind my report on everyday editing tasks.
body: The repository includes a synthetic project plan, requests to run against it, and a harness for inspecting the resulting document. The October tests covered checkboxes, suggestions, comments and section moves.

title: Ask for technical options you can understand
description: A coaching habit for comparing implementation options.
body: And then I think one thing that's like very important is like figuring out a way of like asking the AI to like give you technical options in a language that you understand.

title: Let the model interview you
description: A way to begin when the task is hard to specify.
body: Or sometimes just having a conversation of like, I don't know exactly how to specify this task. Can you kind of like ask me questions?

title: Let the model suggest a starting point
description: How I start in a field I don’t know well.
body: And so for the things where you're not a world expert or where you don't have like a bunch of context, it's like very useful to just like let it start by suggesting things for you.

title: Who wants another session?
description: One question I use when deciding where coaching would help.
body: You have to figure out who's eager to work with you further.

title: Change the interview as you learn
description: Why I keep revising the interview questions in a workflow audit.
body: And if you have like 20 calls, there's like enough space that you can iterate and find your way through.

title: What I want an inbox assistant to notice
description: One design choice behind an inbox assistant.
body: Which is just like it should collect all information passively. I don't want to like have to remind it that there's like an email that happened.
